milestones.title: Redesign — paper first
milestones.description: The concept canvas (six boards) built for real: type wall, family page, your-own-text flow, selection and drag, Pairing Studio, motion. Gate: every board matched by eye at 1440×900 in both themes; e2e, a11y and the 60 fps wall budget green.

labels.name: harness:ready
labels.description: Can be picked up by the harness

epics.title: Redesign foundation: targets, fixture, tokens, motion primitives
epics.summary: What every redesign story builds on: the concept boards exported as target images next to the code, a browser-mode library big enough to look like one, the owner's accent per theme, and the motion tokens and transition helpers the later epics reuse. Concept canvas: https://claude.ai/artifact/4EtzdBCYU4LWsxaXNQKvNv — boards 1–6. The design rules live in dev-docs/redesign/DESIGN.md.

stories.title: Export the six concept boards as target images
criteria: dev-docs/design/redesign/ holds the 18 PNGs listed in its README.md (five wall presets, eight family-page states, two your-own-text states, drag, studio, motion), each exported from the concept canvas at 1440 px wide with the Export-state tweak set as the README says; the export date is filled in
Every UI story in E41–E46 links its target image by that path; a story is reviewed against the image, not against the previous screenshot
DESIGN.md's audit section is replaced by a pointer to the boards and a short list of what the boards leave open (dark theme of each board, compact density, narrow windows)

stories.title: Browser-mode library that looks like a library
criteria: `?mockLibrary=wall` (and the default for e2e @screens) serves 60 families across classifications: ≥12 serif, ≥16 sans, 6 slab, 6 script/hand, 6 mono, 8 display, 6 variable (two with 3+ axes), with Cyrillic, Greek and Vietnamese coverage on some and deliberate gaps on others, 3 duplicates and 2 broken files — all from fixtures/fonts/ (OFL/Apache/UFL only)
Families carry realistic designer, foundry, year, licence and style counts; mock `sampleTexts` reports `missing` glyphs for the gap families so tofu rendering can be seen
scripts/redesign/shots.mjs and the @screens spec use the wall library by default; the three-family library stays available as `?mockLibrary=small` for the existing specs that count rows
No change to the FmClient interface or generated types

stories.title: Accent per theme and on-accent token
criteria: `--fm-accent` is #C56EB2 in light and #AB4B96 in dark; a new `--fm-on-accent` is #141413 in light and #ffffff in dark; both pairs ≥ 4.5:1, enforced by styles/contrast.test.ts

Every element that paints text on the accent (primary button, count badge, pressed chip, toast, switch label if any) uses `--fm-on-accent`; accent-coloured text and links go back to `--fm-fg` — grep shows no `color: var(--fm-accent)` on text
Focus ring, selection ring, active segment, switch-on state, slider thumb and the activation toggle take the accent
The @screens set opened in both themes; axe (a11y.spec.ts) green

stories.title: Motion tokens, reduced-motion switch and transition helpers
criteria: theme.css defines `--fm-motion-fast: 120ms`, `--fm-motion-move: 200ms`, `--fm-motion-page: 280ms`, `--fm-ease: cubic-bezier(.2,0,0,1)` and sets all three durations to 0ms under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`; no component declares its own duration or curve (lint rule or grep test)

`src/motion/` exports `useReducedMotion()`, a `<FmFade>` / `<FmSlide>` pair over Vue `<Transition>`, a `<FmFlipGroup>` over `<TransitionGroup>` that animates transform only, and `withViewTransition(fn)` that uses `document.startViewTransition` when present and falls back to running `fn` directly
Only `transform` and `opacity` are animated by the helpers (asserted in a unit test that inspects the generated styles)
Board 6 (6-motion.png) is copied into dev-docs/redesign/MOTION.md as the table the later epics implement against

epics.title: Type wall — the library as designers open it
epics.summary: Board 1. One hero control (type to preview), a uniform wall of white cards on paper that reflows with the size slider, a quiet paper-tinted sidebar, filters as a button plus chips, no inspector on the wall. Target: dev-docs/design/redesign/1-wall-word.png (and 1-wall-pangram/alphabet/numerals/paragraph.png for the presets).

stories.title: The wall: uniform specimen cards that reflow
criteria: Grid view renders families as white cards on #ffffff with a hairline (`--fm-border`) and 12 px radius: specimen centred (the preview text, never truncated — the text shrinks to fit or the card shows the longest prefix that fits on a word boundary), footer with activation dot, family name (500) and style count / Variable in tabular figures

The size slider (24–120) resizes every visible card and the grid reflows through `<FmFlipGroup>`; cards keep identity; off-screen cards jump; 60 fps with 1,000 families in the wall library (measured in e2e with the Performance API, asserted ≥ 55 fps median)
Column count follows width (minmax 260px); at 1440 px that is four columns; the wall stays virtualised in rows
Selected card: 2 px accent ring; hover: shadow lift per the motion table; Enter opens the family page, Space opens Quick Look, A toggles activation, as today
Matches 1-wall-word.png (and 1-wall-pangram/alphabet/numerals/paragraph.png for the presets) at 1440×900 in light and dark (reviewer compares side by side; differences listed in the PR)

stories.title: Preview text as the hero control
criteria: Above the wall: a 44 px text field 'Type to preview' with a hint at its end, preset chips Word · Pangram · Alphabet · Numerals · Paragraph — each a different wall layout as in 1-wall-<preset>.png (4 columns / 2 wide / 2 wrapped / 4 figures / 2 body-text) — then a divider and a Language picker (recent languages first, then all from `listLanguages()`) that puts that language's pangram on the wall

Typing repaints every specimen on the next frame with no transition; the value is shared by list, wall, waterfall, family page and Quick Look, and remembered per view (view preferences in localStorage, as today)

The old preview toolbar's remaining controls (size, auto size, line height, tracking, alignment, metrics, outline, colours, surface) live in a Preview options popover opened from one button at the end of the row; nothing else is on screen by default
Keyboard: `/` focuses search, `T` (when no row is focused) focuses the preview field; Esc returns focus to the wall

stories.title: Sidebar as a quiet paper panel
criteria: Sidebar background `--fm-surface` (paper tint #f6f5f2 light / surface-2 dark), 232 px, hairline on its right; rows 30 px with a 16 px Lucide icon, label and a right-aligned tabular count; the active row has the 7 % tint
Section headers are 11 px uppercase with their actions as icon buttons that appear on hover/focus (New collection, Add folder, Import set); no text buttons inline in the list
Collections show a colour dot (E44.3) and smart collections a distinct icon, not a trailing 'Smart' pill; Problems appears once, as a section with its count; empty sections show one quiet line
Bottom row: problems count with its dot and the ⌘K/Ctrl+K hint; app/API/platform versions move to About
Matches the sidebar of 1-wall-word.png (and 1-wall-pangram/alphabet/numerals/paragraph.png for the presets); RTL chrome and compact density verified in @screens

stories.title: Filters as a button and a chip row
criteria: The top bar shows `Filters` with a count badge (accent, on-accent text) that opens the existing drawer; active filters render as removable chips to its right, one row, overflow collapses into '+N'
The chip wall above the list is gone from every view; its facets are all reachable in the drawer (parity checked by the filters e2e spec)
The count line above the wall reads '212 families · Sans serif · Serbian (Latin)' and 'Sorted by name · change'

stories.title: No inspector on the wall
criteria: The wall, list, waterfall and table views no longer show the inspector pane; selecting a row shows its name and state in the count line, Enter or a click on the name opens the family page, Space opens Quick Look
The `]` shortcut and the toolbar inspector toggle are removed from these views; the table view keeps its column menu
Every inspector capability has a home on the family page (E42) — a checklist in the PR maps Info/Axes/Features/Glyphs/Developer/License/Palettes/Notes to their new section
The existing inspector e2e specs are updated to the family page; none deleted

epics.title: Family page — one place for everything about a family
epics.summary: Board 2. Clicking a card pushes a page: hero specimen in your text with the variable axes under it, a segmented switch Styles · Text · Characters · Features · Pairings · Info, and a quiet rail (languages you can preview in, pairs well with, facts). Target: dev-docs/design/redesign/2-family-*.png (one per section; see dev-docs/design/redesign/README.md); the board is interactive — play it for every section.

stories.title: Route, push/pop navigation and the page frame
criteria: `/family/:id` route; opening from any view pushes the page with the shared-element transition from the motion table (fallback: slide + fade); Back (button, Esc, Alt+←) pops it and restores the view's scroll position and selection

Top bar: ‹ Library, '1 of 212 · ← → next family' (arrows move to the previous/next family in the current filtered order without leaving the page), icon buttons Favorite · Add to collection · Tag · Find similar, and the primary 'Activate family' (accent, on-accent)
Page skeleton: hero area, axis row, section switch (`UiSegmentedControl`), a 560+ px main column and a 320 px rail that wraps under it below 1100 px
Deep link works in browser mode for the @screens scene `family`

stories.title: Hero specimen and live axes
criteria: Hero: the preview text at 132 px (clamped to the width, one line, ellipsis) in the family's default face; a meta line with foundry, year, axes/style count, licence and activation state

For a variable family every axis is a slider with a numeric readout; dragging updates the hero, the Styles rows and the rail samples on the same frame via `font-variation-settings`; ticks under the weight slider mark the named instances and a label reads '= Medium' within ±12 or 'between instances'
Dragging horizontally on the hero specimen scrubs the weight axis (pointer capture; 1 px = 2 units; Shift halves); the cursor shows ew-resize
'Pin 537 as my instance' calls the existing `pinInstance` and the new style appears in Styles; 'Copy CSS' puts `font-variation-settings` on the clipboard via `cssValues`

stories.title: Styles: named list and weight ramp
criteria: Named styles: one row per face — name and weight/italic meta (150 px), the preview text at 38 px, hover actions Copy CSS · Compare, and an activation switch (`role=switch`, accent when on) that calls activate/deactivate for that face

A `Named styles · N | Weight ramp` switch (variable families only) shows the weight axis at every 100 with the instance name where one exists; clicking a ramp row sets the hero weight; the accent ring on both lists follows the current hero weight (±12)
Pinned instances (`listVirtualStyles`) appear in the named list with a 'yours' badge and can be deleted from the row menu
Keyboard: ↑/↓ move between rows, Space toggles activation, Enter sets the hero to that row's weight

stories.title: Text section: the reading test
criteria: Three columns of the same passage at 12 / 17 / 24 px labelled captions · body · lead, line height 1.45, `opsz` set to the size where the family has the axis
Measure (40–90 ch) and leading (1.10–1.80) sliders apply to all three; a Paper | Ink switch flips the section to light-on-dark; an ink block below shows the body size on `--fm-fg` ground
The passage is the user's preview text when it is longer than 80 characters, otherwise the stock passage; the Paragraph preset from E41.2 lands here

stories.title: Characters section: grid, blocks and glyph detail
criteria: A 12-column glyph grid from `listGlyphs` in the family's face at 26 px, virtualised, with block filter chips (count per block) and a search that accepts a character, `U+017D` or a glyph name (`getGlyph`)

Selecting a cell (click, arrows, Enter) shows the detail card: the glyph at 160 px, name, code point, 'in N of M styles', and its alternates rendered live (stylistic sets and axis extremes from `GlyphDetail`); Copy glyph and 'Compare with…' (existing GlyphCompare)
No inner scrollbars: the grid grows with the page; the detail card is sticky on tall windows
Matches the Characters state of board 2

stories.title: Features section: off and on, side by side
criteria: Each non-automatic feature from `FeatureInfo` is a row: friendly name with the tag in mono under it, the sample rendered without the feature (muted) and with it (`font-feature-settings`), and a switch
Switched-on features apply to every preview on the page (hero, Styles, Text) through the shared preview state; 'Copy CSS for N switched on' writes the `font-feature-settings` line

Samples are chosen per feature from data/features (E42.11): ligature words for `liga`/`dlig`, mixed case for `smcp`/`c2sc`, digits for `onum`/`tnum`/`pnum`/`lnum`, fractions for `frac`; stylistic sets fall back to the preview text
Rare tags (cvXX, locl, mark…) sit behind an 'N more' expander

stories.title: Pairings section: candidates from your library
criteria: Four to eight cards from `suggestPairings`, each a mini layout — this family as the headline (30 px) over the candidate as body (14 px) — with the candidate's name and its `reasons` joined by ' · '
A `This family for headlines | for body` switch sends the role to the request and swaps which face plays which part in the cards
Clicking a card opens the Studio with the pairing loaded (E45.2); hovering lifts the card per the motion table
Empty state when the library has no candidate: one line and an action to browse catalogs

stories.title: Info section: design, licence, files, metrics
criteria: Four groups in a two-column grid: Design (designer, foundry · year, classification, axes with ranges, named styles, description), Licence (name, 'You may' and 'You may not' lines from `LicenseInfo.permissions`, the user's record with a link to declare), Files (format, location, added, health), Metrics (units/em, cap, x-height with ratio, ascender, descender)
Metrics show an 'Hxg' specimen at 96 px with dashed accent lines at cap height and x-height and a solid baseline, drawn from the face's metrics
Hash, name IDs, vendor ID and the full table list stay in the Developer section, reachable from a 'Technical details' expander at the end of the rail

stories.title: The rail: preview in a language, pairs well with, facts
criteria: 'Supports N languages': only complete languages from `faceCoverage` as chips (six, then '+N more' expands); clicking a chip sets the page's preview text to that language's pangram (`LanguagePreset.pangram`) and marks the chip with the accent; clicking again or 'back to my text' restores the user's text
Under the chips a 22 px line of the language's distinctive glyphs (from data/charsets) rendered in the face — never a fallback font (missing glyphs would be tofu per E43.4)
'Pairs well with': the top two from `suggestPairings` with one reason each and 'Open in Pairing Studio'
Facts grid: designer, foundry, licence with web/embed marks, format/files/size, 'Used in' linking to collections that contain the family; 'Technical details' expander at the end
Choosing a language here also offers 'Show only fonts that can do Polish' which applies the language filter when going back to the wall

stories.title: Language samples: distinctive glyph lines per language
criteria: data/charsets/<lang>.json gains an optional `sampleGlyphs` string (the language's distinctive letters, e.g. 'Šđčćž' for sr-Latn, 'Ąćęłńóśźż' for pl) and the schema and validation test accept it; the 30 most used presets are filled
`LanguagePreset` gains `sampleGlyphs?: string | null` (additive, `#[serde(default)]`); `pnpm gen:types` output committed
Pangrams exist for every preset that has `sampleGlyphs` (data/pangrams); missing ones added for sr-Latn, sr-Cyrl, hr, bs, sl, mk

stories.title: Feature catalog: friendly names, groups and samples
criteria: data/features/features.json (schema-validated) lists every registered OpenType feature tag with a friendly name, a group (Ligatures · Capitals · Figures · Fractions · Positioning · Stylistic · Language · Automatic) and a sample string; the fm-core feature reader uses it for `FeatureInfo.name` and gains `group` and `sample` (additive fields)
A unit test checks every tag the fixture corpus exposes has a name; `cvXX`/`ssXX` without a font-supplied name fall back to 'Character variant 3' / 'Stylistic set 1'
`pnpm gen:types` output committed

stories.title: Licence permissions summary in fm-core
criteria: `LicenseInfo` gains `permissions?: LicensePermissions | null` with `may: string[]`, `mayNot: string[]`, `source: 'open-license' | 'declared' | 'embedding-bits'` — derived in fm-core from the recognised open licence (OFL, Apache, UFL, MIT…), the user's declaration and `fsType`; never invented when nothing is known (null)
Rules live in data/licenses/permissions.json (schema-validated) so wording is editable without code changes
Unit tests cover OFL, Apache-2.0, UFL, a declared desktop licence and a restricted-embedding file
Additive change to fm-api: no existing field renamed or removed; `pnpm gen:types` output committed

stories.title: Role-aware pairing suggestions
criteria: `PairingRequest` gains `role?: 'headline' | 'body' | 'caption'` (default: as today) and `partnerOf?: FaceId` for 'given this body face, suggest headlines'; scoring weights contrast, x-height ratio, width and era differently per role, documented in docs/adr/ as an amendment to the pairing ADR
`PairingSuggestion.reasons` stay plain words and become role-specific ('lower contrast for body', 'x-height within 4 %')
Bench: suggestions for one face against the 10k reference library return in < 50 ms (search budget)
Additive change; `pnpm gen:types` output committed

epics.title: Your own text and honest rendering
epics.summary: Board 3. Type a sentence in your language and the wall becomes reading rows at real body size; fonts that cannot render every glyph say so with visible tofu, and one switch hides them. Target: dev-docs/design/redesign/3-wall-text.png and 3-wall-text-complete.png.

stories.title: Paragraph mode: reading rows when the text is long
criteria: When the preview text exceeds 80 characters or the Paragraph preset is chosen, the wall switches to two-column rows: family name and meta in a 12 px line, the text at the body size (default 17 px / 1.45; the Preview options size applies), 18 px padding, same card chrome
The switch animates as a view crossfade (motion table); switching back restores the wall and its scroll position
The count line reads 'N of M families render your text completely' when the text has glyphs outside Basic Latin
Matches 3-wall-text.png and 3-wall-text-complete.png

stories.title: Script detection for typed text
criteria: `detect_languages(text) -> Vec<LanguageHint { code, confidence }>` in fm-core, exposed through fm-api as `detectLanguages`, using the charsets data: a text whose distinctive glyphs match a preset's `sampleGlyphs`/required set ranks that preset first (sr-Latn before hr before pl for 'đ' + 'ć'); pure ASCII returns an empty list
Unit tests for Serbian Latin, Serbian Cyrillic, Polish, Vietnamese, Greek and mixed text; < 1 ms per call
`pnpm gen:types` output committed

stories.title: Renders-my-text filter with a count
criteria: When the text has non-ASCII glyphs the field's end label reads '<Language> detected · showing fonts that render every glyph' from `detectLanguages`; the count line gets a switch 'Hide the N with missing glyphs' that applies `Supports { kind: 'text' }` to the search
The switch state is a filter chip like any other (removable, shown in the Filters badge count) and is remembered with the view
Performance: toggling on the 1,000-family wall library re-renders in < 100 ms (search budget + paint) measured in e2e

stories.title: Tofu: missing glyphs drawn, never faked
criteria: Every specimen renderer (wall card, list row, waterfall, family hero and rows, Quick Look, Studio) takes the `missing` characters from `sampleTexts` and renders each as an inline box: 0.62 em wide, 1.5 px accent border, 2 px radius, light accent fill; the box is an element with `role=img` and `aria-label="missing glyph ž"`
The row/card shows 'N glyphs missing · š đ č' in the accent colour; the family page shows the same under the hero
No specimen anywhere falls back to a system font for a missing character (a Playwright check compares the rendered width of a known-missing string against the tofu width)
Matches the gap rows of 3-wall-text.png and 3-wall-text-complete.png

epics.title: Selection, drag and collections
epics.summary: Board 4. Select several families, act on them from a bar that rises from the bottom, drag them onto a collection, a tag or the Studio with a ghost and a count, and drag them out of the app as files. Target: dev-docs/design/redesign/4-drag.png.

stories.title: Multi-select model and the selection bar
criteria: Click selects one; Shift-click a range; Ctrl/Cmd-click toggles; dragging on the wall's empty ground draws a box that selects what it touches; Esc clears; Ctrl/Cmd-A selects the filtered set; selection survives view switches
Selected cards/rows: accent ring and a 6 % accent tint; the count line reads 'N selected · Shift-click or drag a box to select · Esc clears'

On the first selection a dark bar (#141413, on it white) rises from the bottom centre per the motion table: 'N families' · Activate · Collection · Tag · Compare · Studio · ×; each action applies to the whole selection through the existing client calls; the bar is a `role=toolbar` reachable with Tab
Matches 4-drag.png minus the drag ghost

stories.title: Drag families onto collections, tags and the Studio
criteria: Dragging a selected card lifts a ghost (the card at 0.9 scale, −3°, shadow, a count badge when more than one) that follows the pointer; the origin cards fade to 35 %

Sidebar collections and tags, and the Studio button in the selection bar, are drop targets: entering one shows the accent ring and the count as '31 → 34'; dropping calls `addToCollection` / `tagFaces` / opens the Studio with the faces; the ghost flies into the row and the count crossfades (motion table)
Smart collections are not drop targets and say why in a tooltip; Esc cancels a drag
Keyboard equivalent exists for every drop (the selection bar's Collection and Tag menus)

stories.title: Collection colours
criteria: `Collection` gains `color?: string | null` (a key from a fixed palette of eight, not a hex) and `createCollection` / `renameCollection` accept it (additive); stored in the database with a migration
The sidebar shows the colour as an 8 px dot before the name and the collection header uses it for its mini specimen strip; the picker is a row of eight swatches in the collection's menu
`pnpm gen:types` output committed; mock supports it

stories.title: Drag out: drop font files into other apps
criteria: Dragging a selection past the window edge starts a native file drag with the faces' files on Windows (IDataObject CF_HDROP), macOS (NSFilePromiseProvider or NSPasteboard file URLs) and Linux (text/uri-list via GTK/Wayland portal) — behind the `FontActivator`-style trait in fm-platform, one implementation per OS, each with an integration test that a second process receives the paths
Files are referenced in place (rule 2: never copied or moved); Explorer/Finder/Nautilus receive them as a copy
Documented in docs/adr/ with the parity decision; a platform that cannot support it ships the feature disabled with a tooltip, not a `cfg` branch elsewhere

epics.title: Pairing Studio — roles on paper
epics.summary: Board 5. One toolbar, the context as a segmented switch, the pairing as four roles in a rail with real font pickers and locks, the page on paper at realistic scale, role marks only on hover or selection, shuffle the unlocked roles, suggestions with reasons, compare two pairings, export. Target: dev-docs/design/redesign/5-studio.png.

stories.title: One toolbar and context presets
criteria: The Studio's four bars become one: Back · 'Pairing Studio' · '<Headline> + <Body> · unsaved' · context switch (Magazine · Web hero · Mobile UI · Video title · Poster) · Compare 2 pairings · Shuffle unlocked · Save · Export

Each context is a real layout from `layoutPresets`/layout templates with the right page: A4 (Magazine, Poster), 1440×900 web hero, 390×844 mobile with iOS type sizes, 1920×1080 video title with safe-area guides
The page sits on a neutral ground (`#ecebe7` light / surface-2 dark) with a soft shadow at 100 % scale by default; the hint line under it says how to hover, select and drag
Matches the toolbar and page of 5-studio.png

stories.title: Roles rail with font pickers and locks
criteria: A 300 px rail lists the context's roles (Magazine: Headline, Deck, Body, Caption; each context defines its own) as cards: role name, lock toggle, a font picker (`UiSelect` with the family rendered in itself and a search over the library), style and size/leading

Role blocks on the page carry no marks at rest; hovering a block shows its role mark in the margin and a hairline ring; clicking selects it (accent ring and mark) and focuses its card in the rail; the rail card's ring follows selection
Drag sideways on a selected block for size, up/down for leading (existing behaviour, kept); Enter edits the block text
Opening the Studio from a pairing card (E42.7) or a drop (E44.2) fills Headline and Body

stories.title: Shuffle unlocked and suggestions with reasons
criteria: 'Shuffle unlocked' asks `suggestPairings` with the locked roles as `partnerOf` and the role as `role`, picks the next candidate for each unlocked role and animates the change (crossfade of the block)
Under the roles a 'Try for <selected role>' list shows three candidates with their reasons; clicking applies to that role only; a shuffled result can be undone (Ctrl/Cmd-Z)
Suggestions come from the user's library only; an empty library state links to catalogs

stories.title: Compare two pairings, save, export
criteria: 'Compare 2 pairings' duplicates the page side by side (two panels, independent roles, shared text); the toolbar label names both; closing one keeps the other
Save stores the pairing as a layout (existing `saveLayout`) named after its faces; History and Revert keep working
Export offers PNG (via E45.5) and PDF (existing print) at 1× and 2×; the file is named '<Headline>-<Body>-<context>.png'

stories.title: Render a layout to PNG in fm-core
criteria: `exportLayoutPng(req: { layout: LayoutId, scale: 1 | 2, surface: 'paper' | 'ink' }) -> path` renders the layout with the core rasterizer (same engine as `renderPreview`), honouring axes and features, into the app's export folder; returns the path
Output matches the webview within tolerance on the fixture layouts (pixel diff < 2 % on a 1× A4 render)
< 1 s for an A4 page at 2× on the reference machine; additive fm-api change; `pnpm gen:types` output committed

epics.title: Motion — everything moves for a reason
epics.summary: Board 6: the twelve moments in dev-docs/redesign/MOTION.md, built on the E40.4 helpers, each with its reduced-motion fallback and a frame budget. Target: dev-docs/design/redesign/6-motion.png.

stories.title: Family page push and pop
criteria: Opening a family: the card's specimen is the shared element that scales into the hero position while the wall fades under it and the top bar crossfades (View Transitions API with `view-transition-name` per card; fallback: 24 px slide + fade), 280 ms `--fm-ease`
Back reverses it at 220 ms with the exit curve and lands on the same scroll position; ← → between families crossfade the page content only (200 ms)
Reduced motion: a 120 ms fade; verified by an e2e test that emulates `prefers-reduced-motion`

stories.title: Wall reflow, view switch and size slider
criteria: Size slider and column-count changes reflow the visible cards with FLIP (transform only), 200 ms; cards entering the viewport appear without animation
Switching view modes crossfades the two lists (200 ms) while the segmented thumb slides (120 ms)
Measured ≥ 55 fps median during a 24→120 slider sweep with the 1,000-family library; the measurement is an e2e test that fails under budget

stories.title: Drawers, popovers, selection bar, toasts
criteria: Filters drawer: translateX from −100 % plus a 6 % scrim, 200 ms; popovers and `UiSelect` lists: 120 ms fade + 4 px rise; selection bar: 16 px rise + fade, 200 ms; toasts the same
All through `<FmFade>`/`<FmSlide>`; no component-local keyframes (grep test)
Reduced motion: fades only

stories.title: Drag, activation, Quick Look and Studio moments
criteria: Drag: ghost lift 120 ms (scale .9, −3°, shadow), drop flies into the target in 200 ms and the count crossfades; activation: dot scale 0→1 and switch knob translate in 120 ms; Quick Look: 200 ms fade + 8 px rise over a fixed (not animated) backdrop blur, ← → crossfade 120 ms; Studio open: paper scale .98→1 + rail slide, 280 ms

Nothing animates while the user types in the preview field, in search results, on the Table view, or when focus moves by keyboard (ring appears at once) — asserted in e2e by checking computed transitions
Reduced motion fallbacks per MOTION.md

epics.title: Themes — Paper and friends
epics.summary: A small set of named themes the user picks in Settings, Slack-style: each is one token set (accent, on-accent, surfaces) with light and dark variants; the current pair is 'Paper' and stays the default. The theme id is a setting, so the model is an API change first.

stories.title: Theme model in settings
criteria: `Settings` gains `themeId?: string` (default 'paper') next to the existing `theme` (system/light/dark, unchanged); `updateSettings` accepts it; additive, with a migration default

Built-in theme definitions live in data/themes/*.json (schema-validated): id, name, light and dark token sets for accent, on-accent, bg, surface, surface-2, border; at least Paper, Graphite (neutral), Indigo, Moss — each pair checked ≥ 4.5:1 by a test
`listThemes()` returns them; `pnpm gen:types` output committed

stories.title: Theme picker that previews the specimens
criteria: Settings › Appearance shows the themes as cards with a live mini wall (three specimens on the theme's surface, its accent on a selected card) in the current light/dark mode; choosing one writes the tokens onto `:root` at once with a 200 ms crossfade and saves `themeId`
The command palette offers 'Theme: <name>'; the choice survives a restart (reads from settings, not localStorage)
Every @screens scene renders correctly under every built-in theme (a loop in the screens spec, run on the review pass)
